title: World Physical Geography: The Face of the Planet

questions.question: The largest continent by area is:
questions.rationale: Continents in decreasing area: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia. Asia also holds both the highest point (Everest) and the lowest exposed land (Dead Sea shore).

questions.question: The longest continental mountain chain in the world is the:
questions.rationale: The Andes stretch about 7,000 km down western South America - the longest continental range. The Himalayas hold the highest peaks but are shorter end to end.

questions.question: The 'roof of the world', the largest and highest plateau, is the:
questions.rationale: The Tibetan Plateau averages about 4,500 m and covers around 2.5 million sq km - its summer heating is a principal driver of the Indian monsoon.

questions.question: Which river crosses the Equator twice?
questions.rationale: The Congo rises south of the Equator, crosses it northward, loops through the rainforest and crosses back southward - a drainage basin lying almost entirely on the Equator.

questions.question: The driest desert in the world is the:
questions.rationale: Chile's Atacama combines a double rain shadow (Andes) with the cold Humboldt current's stabilising air - some weather stations have never recorded meaningful rain.

questions.question: The strait through which about a fifth of the world's petroleum passes is:
questions.rationale: The Strait of Hormuz gates the Persian Gulf; tankers carrying roughly 20% of global oil must thread it. Malacca is China's general energy lifeline from Africa and the Gulf.

questions.question: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, connects:
options: The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Black Sea and Caspian Sea
questions.rationale: Suez links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, saving ships the Cape of Good Hope rounding - about 7,000 km between Europe and Asia. Panama (Atlantic-Pacific) and Kiel (Baltic-North Sea) are the other great canal shortcuts.

questions.question: The largest lake in the world by area is the:
questions.rationale: The Caspian, a salt lake, is the largest by area. Baikal is the deepest (and largest by volume of fresh water), Superior the largest freshwater lake by area, and Victoria Africa's largest lake.

questions.question: The Vosges and Black Forest are examples of:
questions.rationale: They are fault-bounded uplifted blocks flanking the Rhine rift - block mountains. Fold mountains are young and high (Himalayas, Alps); residual ones are worn-down ancient masses (Aravallis, Urals, Appalachians).

questions.question: The deepest known point of the world's oceans lies in the:
questions.rationale: The Challenger Deep in the western Pacific's Mariana Trench reaches about 11,000 m - deeper than Everest is tall. All four options are hadal trenches, but the Mariana is the standard exam answer for the deepest.
